quest.title: Sightlines and Camera Tricks
quest.description: A special training ground has been set up in the southern section of Lumidouce Harbor in Fontaine...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: ...Terminal ballistics are impeccable, and the dispersion is close to the ideal.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: According to our assessment models here at the Maison Gardiennage's weapons bureau, your weapon is very much a "cannon."

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: It's just a shame that we'd need at least two teams' worth of manpower to deploy your "musket" in the field. It's too complicated to use...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Thank you for the approval, Officer Chevreuse. Actually, I don't think the high barrier to entry's a bad thing. Before I had the "Soulsniper: Ritual Staff" custom-made by Xilonen, we agreed that...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: "The stronger the weapon, the stricter its usage standards should be."

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Apart from their difficulty of use, I've even considered placing a "moral cognition-based lock" on such weapons.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: That way, we can ensure they are wielded by the right people, preventing any immense damage resulting from criminal theft.

dialogues.speaker: Turenna
dialogues.text: That's a fair concern, Officer Chasca. Weapon theft that leads to committed crimes is not uncommon here in Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, so many old friends!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fontaine's Maison Gardiennage, Natlan's "Flower-Feather Clan"... and a Knight of Favonius? What's going on with this little gathering of yours?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Reconvening the multilateral exchange?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Another joint wargame?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: #Bullseye. You caught on to the situation immediately, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Some time back, the Special Patrol sent Turenna to Liyue to take part in a joint wargame. That wargame became the catalyst for ever more frequent exchanges between the armed forces of various nations.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: This time around, it's the routine "Ballistic Wargame" between Fontaine and Mondstadt — aimed at sharpening combatants' battlefield-planning capabilities on all sides.

dialogues.speaker: Turenna
dialogues.text: And this time, thanks to our friends in the Knights of Favonius putting in a good word, the warriors of Natlan's "Flower-Feather Clan" have joined the wargame as well.

dialogues.speaker: Turenna
dialogues.text: The Flower-Feather Clan warriors are skilled at firing while in flight — they've opened the doors to a whole new world for us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... The Knights must have gotten to know the Natlanese warriors during their expedition, then? Paimon should've thought of that sooner!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But what's a "Ballistic Wargame," really? Paimon understands every word individually, but put them together and it gets a little confusing...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Doesn't shooting just mean firing the gun and being done with it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are bullets allowed in wargames too?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Aha, if everyone had unlimited ammunition, you'd just hold down the trigger, and most enemies would be no problem at all.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: But combat is a long-drawn-out process. A shooter can only carry so much ammunition, so every shot needs to land — and to land strategically.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: So the Knights of Favonius have developed a new type of grenade to help shooters sharpen their understanding. The principle behind it is a little complicated, though...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: As for the specifics, I'll let our friend from the Knights of Favonius walk you through it.

dialogues.speaker: Hedwig
dialogues.text: #Coming, coming — apologies! I was buried in report-organizing and hadn't even noticed the Honorary Knight and {M#his}{F#her} little white companion. My greetings to you both!

dialogues.speaker: Hedwig
dialogues.text: I'm Hedwig, member of the Knights of Favonius's General Affairs Company. I'm in charge of recording proceedings for this wargame, and coordinating between the gunsmiths and our other allies...

dialogues.speaker: Hedwig
dialogues.text: Speaking of which — the device for this round actually has a connection to you two. Do you remember the strange Samachurl statue that once appeared in Dadaupa Gorge?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Vaguely. Long time ago, that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't remember. Doesn't matter, does it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even Paimon's a bit fuzzy on it. Hedwig, why don't you give us the short version?

dialogues.speaker: Hedwig
dialogues.text: Right then. I'll skip past the old legends and the scattered intel and cut to it —

dialogues.speaker: Hedwig
dialogues.text: According to the Investigation Company's findings, that statue was the work of an ancient Samachurl. The "Ladler of Broth" Churldric had taken an unused Domain and reshaped it into a place to drill his battle formations.

dialogues.speaker: Hedwig
dialogues.text: The Honorary Knight defeated one of Churldric's lingering shadows back then, which caused the Domain to collapse — and the "Eyes of Upano" that oversaw the formations scattered out into the open.

dialogues.speaker: Hedwig
dialogues.text: Once the Support Company had a sample in hand, they spent the better part of a year carefully disassembling and analyzing it. Eventually they got the technology figured out, combined it with the design principles of Liyue's overhead surveillance devices...

dialogues.speaker: Hedwig
dialogues.text: ...And produced a kind of visualizing "observation grenade" — meant for long-range reconnaissance, so a shooter can gather information from a position of safety.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a roundabout journey... Paimon never imagined that little fellow we wrapped up without much fanfare would leave behind such a mysterious treasure!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: The upshot is, in a wargame setting, the "observation grenade" lets shooters see through the eyes of the round in flight — deepening their grasp of trajectory and obstacles...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: ...So they can practice shooting strategies geared toward different scenarios. It works on quite a few clever little angles!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: As for us Flower-Feather Clan members, our Saurian-riders often have difficulty determining the effects of shots we make while riding our Qucusaurs. We are up in the sky, after all, with our targets being far away...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: These observation grenades can thus help us conduct battlefield damage assessments... That's a term I learned from the Special Patrol, by the by — it's a very concise concept.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: At present, the people involved in the wargame have completed everything our two leaders, Chasca and Chevreuse, have designated for them.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: All that's left is to complete our wargame with an expanded sample.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Since you're here, Honorary Knight, would you like to try it out?

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: I did notice during the Fontinalia Film Festival that you're quite a crack shot, and an inspired one, too.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: #I'm personally interested to see how much your marksmanship's improved over the years, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: And from the perspective of the wargame, your lack of familiarity with the observation grenades means that you can form an excellent control group for us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Heh. Y'know, {NICKNAME}... It does feel like this grenade thing has real history with us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Might as well try its effects for ourselves, eh? It should be pretty fun!

choices.text: Guess I'll have to step up and take this seriously.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Totally! An extra skill's an extra skill, right? Never know if we'll run into some sorta... bad guy who can only be taken out with muskets or something!

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Great! In that case, I'll prepare the venue and notify all those we have playing as targets!

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: The rules are simple: Make as few "adjustments" as possible while defeating your targets efficiently...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I should first say that this drill was made to be tough. Even the Special Patrol's previous marksmanship instructor, Enghiene, was barely able to pass...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: But I suspect you'll do just fine.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Of course, there's no need to feel pressured. Sometimes, shooting is not just about technique, but also about inspiration that arrives as light as feathers, and a little luck to send it off on the wind.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Don't think of this as a test, but more as a relaxing game. Perhaps you'll gain something unexpected from all this, hmm?

choices.text: A bit of marksmanship practice is good for me too.
